questions.stem: Why do red blood cells lack a nucleus?

options.text: To provide more space for haemoglobin, which carries oxygen
To reduce their need for energy from respiration
To allow them to change shape more easily
To help them move faster through blood vessels

questions.explanation: Red blood cells have lost their nucleus during differentiation to create more space for haemoglobin, the protein that binds to and carries oxygen from the lungs to body tissues.
